annotations.cancer_association_rationale: ALK is a receptor tyrosine kinase implicated in cancer primarily through rearrangements (structural variants) that generate oncogenic fusion proteins. The most prevalent fusion in NSCLC is EML4-ALK, which occurs via paracentric inversion of chromosome 2p and retains the ALK kinase domain fused to EML4 coiled-coil domains that drive constitutive oligomerization and activation of oncogenic signaling. EML4-ALK variants (V1, V2, V3, and others) show differential clinical responses to ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitors (crizotinib, ceritinib, lorlatinib, alectinib), with compound ALK mutations conferring resistance to sequential inhibitor therapy. ALK rearrangements also occur in renal cell carcinoma and represent an emerging therapeutic target in that context. Evidence types include structural variants (fusion proteins), differential expression and signaling dependent on fusion variant, and resistance mutations arising during targeted therapy.

annotations.gene_summary: ALK is a receptor tyrosine kinase that functions as an oncogenic driver when rearranged into fusion proteins, most commonly EML4-ALK in NSCLC (PMID 27573755). EML4-ALK fusions result from paracrine inversion of chromosome 2p that fuses the ALK kinase domain to EML4 coiled-coil domains, generating constitutively active signaling complexes that orchestrate oncogenic output through MAPK, PI3K, and PLCγ pathways (PMID 34661367). Multiple EML4-ALK variants (V1, V3, V2, and others) exist with distinct clinical responses to ALK inhibitors; sequential therapy with increasingly potent inhibitors can select for compound ALK mutations conferring high-level resistance (PMID 29650534). ALK rearrangements have been identified as drivers in renal cell carcinoma, with EML4-ALK fusion demonstrating tumorigenic capacity that is reversed by ALK-specific inhibitor crizotinib (PMID 32020234). (Literature sourced via Tier 1 direct PubMed query.)

supporting_quotes.quote: A wide variety of ALK fusions, in which the kinase domain of ALK and the amino-terminal portion of various protein partners are fused, occur in cancer, with echinoderm microtubule-associated protein-like 4 (EML4)-ALK being the most prevalent in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Different ALK fusion proteins can mediate different signalling outputs, depending on properties such as subcellular localisation and protein stability.

EML4-ALK V1 and V3 proteins form cytoplasmic foci that contain components of the MAPK, PLCγ and PI3K signalling pathways...EML4-ALK foci formation occurs as a result of transient association of stable EML4-ALK trimers mediated through an active conformation of the ALK kinase domain.

Sequential ALK inhibitors can foster the emergence of compound ALK mutations that confer high-level resistance to ALK-targeted therapies. Treatment with sequential first-, second-, and third-generation ALK inhibitors can select for compound ALK mutations that confer high-level resistance to ALK-targeted therapies.

Yes — EML4::ALK is a definitively oncogenic, gain-of-function driver fusion, not a variant of uncertain significance. Two distinct classification axes apply, and they should not be conflated:
- Biological oncogenicity: Oncogenic (highest tier) under somatic oncogenicity frameworks (ClinGen/CGC/VICC). It is an activating structural rearrangement of a proto-oncogene with demonstrated transforming capacity in vitro and tumor-initiating capacity in vivo.[[1]][[2]][[3]]
- Clinical actionability: In NSCLC, AMP/ASCO/CAP Tier I, Level A — a biomarker predicting response to an FDA-approved therapy with FDA-approved companion diagnostics[[4]]. Equivalently OncoKB Level 1 and ESCAT tier I. This designation is disease-context–specific to ALK-positive NSCLC and does not extend automatically to other tum[[5]][[6]][[7]]or types.
Mechanism
A paracentric inversion of chromosome 2p, inv(2)(p21p23), joins 5′ EML4 to 3′ ALK, retaining the entire ALK tyrosine kinase domain.[[8]][[9]] The ALK breakpoint is canonically in intron 19; EML4 breakpoints vary, generating variants V1 (E13;A20), V3a/b (E6;A20), V2 (E20;A20) and others, with V1 and V3 accounting for 75–80%.[[10]][[11]] All retain the EML4 trimerization/coiled-coil domain, which drives ligand-independent oligomerization, ALK autophosphorylation, and constitutive signaling through RAS/MAPK, PI3K–AKT and JAK–STAT.[[8]][[12]][[13]] EML4-ALK also forms cytoplasmic condensates via phase separation, which is required for full downstream signaling and tumorigenesis.[[13]][[14]]
Strongest supporting evidence, by strength of causal inference
[[1]][[2]][[3]][[11]][[15]][[16]][[17]][[18]][[19]][[20]][[21]]
The functional and murine genetic data establish causation (the fusion is sufficient to initiate lung adenocarcinoma); the randomized trials establish continued dependency in humans. Note that the phase 3 trials enrolled patients by ALK IHC/FISH positivity rather than transcript-level EML4 confirmation, so they demonstrate ALK-fusion dependency broadly, with EML4 as the partner in roughly 83% of ALK-rearranged NSCLC.[[22]] Six ALK TKIs are FDA-approved in ALK-positive NSCLC, and NCCN lists alectinib, brigatinib, ensartinib and lorlatinib as preferred category 1 first-line options.[[23]][[24]]
Important qualifiers
- Oncogenicity requires a productive fusion. The alteration must be in-frame, expressed, and retain both the ALK kinase domain and the 5′ partner's oligomerization domain. A break-apart FISH signal or a DNA-level rearrangement call alone does not establish this.[[5]][[25]] NCCN notes that any variant classified as a VUS should not be used as the basis for targeted therapy selection, and that RNA-based NGS is recommended when DNA-based profiling identifies no driver, since it directly demonstrates the fusion transcript. D5F3 IHC confirms ALK protein expression but does not identify the partner or the exact breakpoint.[[23]]
- Variants are not biologically uniform. A 2025 meta-analysis of 30 studies (n=2,737) found V3 associated with shorter PFS on ALK TKIs than V1 (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.17–1.99), with no significant difference in OS or ORR. V3 is en[[26]]riched for ALK G1202R at resistance and, in the GuardantINFORM real-world cohort, the V3/TP53-mutant combination had the shortest time to first-line TKI discontinuation (median 7.4 mo). In autochthonous mouse models V3 was more oncogenic than V1, with variant-specific tumor suppressor interactions. Findings are heterogeneous across cohorts and confounded by T[[27]][[28]][[29]]KI generation and co-alterations, so variant status is not currently a basis for altering first-line therapy.
- Non-canonical breakpoints in ALK intron 17 or 18 yield less stable, more weakly signaling fusion proteins with reduced TKI sensitivity — an argument for transcript-level characterization when an atypical fusion is reported.[[25]]
- Outside NSCLC, ALK fusions are drivers in ALCL (usually NPM1::ALK, 50–80%) and [inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor](/rare-disease/inflammatory-myofibroblastic-tumor) (~50%), but EML4 is the partner in only ~31% of non-NSCLC ALK-rearranged tumors, and ALK rearrangement overall occurs in ~0.2% of non-NSCLC cancers. There is no tumor-agnostic ALK approval; the NCI-M[[22]][[30]]ATCH subprotocol F experience was very small.[[31]]


Would you like to explore how to resolve discordant or equivocal ALK results between IHC, FISH, and DNA-based NGS?

annotations.cancer_association_rationale: Structural variant (fusion): EML4-ALK is a recurrent oncogenic fusion arising from paracentric inversion of chromosome 2p, joining the 5′ EML4 trimerization domain to the 3′ ALK tyrosine kinase domain. Multiple EML4-ALK variants (V1, V2, V3, etc.) differ by exon breakpoints and show variant-specific effects on oncogenicity, protein stability, and drug sensitivity. The fusion drives constitutive ALK kinase activity and is the dominant ALK fusion partner (~85% of ALK+ NSCLC). Clinical dependence is established across multiple randomized trials (ALEX, CROWN) showing durable responses to ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitors, with median progression-free survival exceeding 5 years in metastatic NSCLC and adjuvant benefit in resected stage IB–IIIA disease.

annotations.gene_summary: EML4 encodes an echinoderm microtubule-associated protein-like 4 that is recurrently fused to the anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) gene in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) through a paracentric chromosome 2 inversion (PMID 40986428). The EML4-ALK fusion protein retains the EML4 trimerization domain and functional ALK tyrosine kinase domain, driving constitutive RTK signaling through biomolecular condensate formation that enhances ligand-independent kinase activity (PMID 40875402). Multiple EML4-ALK variants exist with distinct breakpoints; variant 3 (V3) is more oncogenic than variant 1 (V1) in autochthonous mouse models and is associated with worse prognosis and higher metastatic risk in patients (PMID 40986428, PMID 37149843). EML4-ALK-positive NSCLC shows durable clinical responses to ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., alectinib, brigatinib, lorlatinib), with median progression-free survival of 34.8 months with alectinib versus 10.9 months with crizotinib in the ALEX trial, superior across all EML4-ALK variants (PMID 30902613). Resistance can emerge through ALK kinase domain point mutations (e.g., G1202R), with V3 showing higher propensity for developing this solvent-front mutation (PMID 37149843). Co-occurring TP53 mutations further influence treatment response and prognosis (PMID 39019326). (Literature sourced via Tier 1 direct PubMed query.)

supporting_quotes.quote: Diverse fusions of echinoderm microtubule-associated protein-like 4 (EML4) and anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) are oncogenic drivers in lung adenocarcinoma. EML4-ALK variants have distinct breakpoints within EML4, but their functional differences remain poorly understood... we show that variant 3 (V3) is more oncogenic than variant 1 (V1).

A prominent example is the cancer-causing EML4-ALK fusion protein, which spontaneously forms biomolecular condensates that significantly enhance receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling within the condensate microenvironment.

Investigator-assessed PFS was longer for alectinib than for crizotinib across EML4-ALK variants 1, 2, and 3a/b in plasma and tissue. Alectinib continues to demonstrate superior investigator-assessed PFS versus crizotinib in untreated ALK-positive NSCLC, irrespective of EML4-ALK variant. The median PFS times were 34.8 months with alectinib and 10.9 months with crizotinib.

EML4::ALK is a definitively oncogenic, gain-of-function driver alteration — not a variant of uncertain significance. The canonical fusion arises from a paracentric inversion of chromosome 2p (inv(2)(p21p23)) joining the 5′ portion of EML4 to the 3′ portion of ALK containing the intact tyrosine kinase domain, producing a chimeric kinase that oligomerizes through the retained EML4 trimerization/coiled-coil domain and signals constitutively in a ligand-independent fashion[[1]].[[2]][[3]] Functionally it satisfies every criterion for a bona fide oncogene: transforming in vitro, sufficient to initiate tumors in vivo at endogenous expression levels, and required for tumor maintenance. Clinically it is a Tier I / level A predictive biomarker in NSCLC (OncoKB "Oncogenic," highest therapeutic level), with FDA-approved matched therapies, companion diagnostics, and NCCN category 1 first-line recommendations.[[4]] The classification applies to in-frame, expressed fusion products retaining both the EML4 oligomerization region and a functional ALK kinase domain — a DNA-level rearrangement that is out of frame or non-productive is not automatically oncogenic and warrants RNA-based confirmation.[[5]]
Strongest supporting evidence, by tier
[[2]][[4]][[6]][[7]][[8]][[9]][[10]][[11]][[12]][[13]][[14]]
Clinical dependence in humans
Randomized trials enroll by ALK positivity (IHC/FISH/NGS) rather than by partner gene, so they formally establish dependence for ALK-rearranged NSCLC — a population in which EML4 is the partner in roughly 85% of cases.[[11]]
- ALEX (alectinib vs crizotinib, treatment-naive): median PFS 34.8 vs 10.9 months (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.32–0.58); 5-year OS 62.5% vs 45.5%; final analysis median OS 81.1 vs 54.2 months (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.56–1.08).[[13]][[15]]
- CROWN (lorlatinib vs crizotinib): 5-year PFS rate 60% with median PFS still not reached at 60.2 months' follow-up (HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.13–0.27) — a median PFS exceeding 5 years in metastatic disease.[[14]]
- ALINA (adjuvant alectinib vs platinum chemotherapy in resected stage IB ≥4 cm–IIIA): significant disease-free survival benefit, now a standard of care.[[16]][[17]]
- Guideline codification: NCCN lists alectinib, brigatinib, ensartinib, and lorlatinib as preferred category 1 first-line options; ASCO guidelines recommend offering alectinib, brigatinib, or lorlatinib first-line (evidence strength high, strong recommendation)[[4]].[[18]]
That a molecularly defined subgroup comprising ~5% of lung adenocarcinoma converts from a median survival of months to a median PFS beyond 5 years on a single oral agent directed at the fusion product is the strongest possible human evidence of causal dependence.[[1]][[14]]
Caveats on scope of the classification
- Variant-level biology is not uniform. V1 (E13;A20) and V3 (E6a/b;A20) differ in condensate properties, HSP90 dependence, protein stability, and TKI sensitivity; V3 has been associated with poorer TKI response and worse prognosis in several analyses. An autochthonous mouse study[[5]][[19]] using somatic genome editing found V3 more oncogenic than V1, with variant-specific tumor suppressor gene interactions, arguing the variants behave as distinct oncogenes rather than one entity. Countering this, the ALEX biomarker subgroup analysis found PFS, ORR, and DOR were not affected by variant 1, 2, or [[20]]3a/b, and alectinib outperformed crizotinib across all variants. Treatment selection remains variant-agnostic in[[21]] practice.[[11]]
- Non-canonical breakpoints. Rare fusions with breakpoints in ALK intron 17 or 18 rather than intron 19 show lower fusion protein stability, weaker phosphorylation and downstream signaling, and reduced TKI sensitivity.[[5]]
- Novel partners require functional validation. Oncogenicity of newly described ALK fusions should be confirmed by transformation assays and demonstrated ALK-TKI sensitivity rather than assumed from the rearrangement call alone.[[5]]
